original_title: Still more GTA 6 details from the latest leaked video: traffic cameras, car trackers, and drivers that put up a fight
summary_en: Fresh gameplay footage from the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6 has surfaced, offering a glimpse into some surprisingly detailed mechanics. Players can expect carjacking to be a more involved process, and the world of Vice City is now actively watching your every move.
ai_analysis: These leaked details suggest Rockstar is pushing for greater immersion in GTA 6, making even mundane actions like stealing a car feel more dynamic and consequential.

en.title: GTA 6 Leaks Reveal Drivers Fight Back, Traffic Cameras Track You
en.summary: Fresh gameplay footage from the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6 has surfaced, offering a glimpse into some surprisingly detailed mechanics. Players can expect carjacking to be a more involved process, and the world of Vice City is now actively watching your every move.
en.body:
The ever-flowing stream of unofficial Grand Theft Auto 6 content continues, with a new video offering a closer look at the game's refined mechanics. This latest leak showcases protagonist Jason carjacking a high-end sports car, the Truffade Thrax, in Vice City. While the overall sequence is brief, it highlights two particularly interesting additions: drivers who actively resist and the presence of traffic cameras that can impact your wanted level.

Traditionally, stealing a vehicle in Grand Theft Auto has been a simple matter of approaching a car, often opening the door and yanking the driver out. However, this leaked clip suggests a more interactive and challenging carjacking experience. Jason is seen struggling with the car's owner, implying a button-mashing or QTE-style interaction that drains the player's stamina meter. This detail, previously hinted at in other leaks concerning a new stamina system, suggests that attempting to steal a car when your stamina is low could prove difficult, adding a layer of strategic consideration to even petty crimes.

## Vice City's Watchful Eyes

The video also provides a glimpse into how law enforcement might be more aware of player actions in GTA 6. As Jason speeds away from the carjacking, the HUD briefly displays an icon resembling three connected circles, identified as a traffic camera. Shortly after passing it, the player enters a red zone and immediately gains two wanted stars. This suggests that traffic cameras are not merely cosmetic but are active elements within the game world, capable of identifying and reporting stolen vehicles or other infractions to the authorities. This detail is particularly topical, echoing real-world concerns about surveillance technology and adding a new layer of consequence to high-speed pursuits and illegal activities within the game's urban environment.

## What This Means for Players

For long-time fans of the Grand Theft Auto series, these leaked details are more than just minor graphical improvements; they represent a potential evolution in gameplay depth. The idea that NPCs will put up a fight during carjackings adds a welcome layer of realism and challenge, moving away from the often-passive nature of previous games. Furthermore, the integration of functional traffic cameras that actively contribute to the wanted system promises a more dynamic and responsive police AI, making the streets of Vice City feel more alive and reactive to the player's actions. It hints at a world that is not just a playground but a living, breathing environment with its own rules and consequences, which is exactly what many players hope to see from Rockstar's next blockbuster.

## What's Next

Rockstar Games has not officially commented on the latest leaks, and no release date for Grand Theft Auto 6 has been confirmed beyond a 2025 window. Players will be eagerly awaiting further official details and trailers to see how these mechanics are fully implemented.

content_raw: Another seemingly legit GTA 6 video surfaced today via Cyberleek , this time showing a couple minutes of high-speed driving through Vice City. The clip (which we can't link here, but you can probably find it quickly with some web searches) begins with protagonist Jason ditching a pickup truck and carjacking a "Truffade Thrax," a fancy sportscar that just happens to already contain a driver. After throwing the car's owner into the street, Jason speeds off, taking us from the Vice City airport through some busy streets downtown, onto the highway, and then into an industrial area. It's not the most eventful trip: the player has a wanted level for jacking the ride but isn't caught and barely even causes any damage along the route. There also aren't a metric ton of new details to pore over, but we did spot a few interesting things to note. Drivers struggle You know the drill. Put your elbow through a car window, open the door, drag the driver out into the street, hop in, and speed away. But it looks like in GTA 6, drivers don't just passively let you gank their whips. In the leaked video, we see Jason struggle with the driver—with the leaker probably having to mash a button—before they can be liberated from their ride. We noticed the new stamina system in the original leak video , and wrestling with drivers drains Jason's stamina meter—so it probably won't be a great idea to try it if you're fully depleted. Traffic cameras Good timing, with all the concern about Flock cameras. As Jason speeds away in the stolen car, there's an icon briefly shown in the middle of the highway: three small connected circles. He passes it, we see the HUD briefly indicate that it saw him, and he immediately enters a red zone and gains two wanted stars. Gotta be a highway traffic camera identifying the stolen car. As soon as he's out of the red zone, the wanted stars vanish again. Lojack When Jason enters the stolen car, we see the gas and engine meters we first noticed in the earlier leak, but there's also a red pin icon. When the player stops the car for a few seconds, the pin begins to blink. This looks like a vehicle recovery system like Lojack, so possibly if you steal a car with one of these devices and don't keep moving, cops might show up at your location, even if you don't currently have any wanted stars. Rude business names confirmed I was starting to think Rockstar has matured. In earlier GTA games it seemed like every business was a rude pun—STD Contractors, Spitroasters Meathouse, BJ's Market, Camel Towing, Gruppe Sechs, etc—but apart from a building in an earlier leak that had the word BALLER on the side, I hadn't seen any rude business names in these leaks. In this latest video, the driver speeds past a number of trucks, billboards, and signs, and they seem mostly restrained: Juice Loose, Mattress Madness, Juicy Joes.
